name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in internet-facing applications such as web servers, APIs, or databases to gain initial access.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Attackers execute malicious commands through interpreters like shell, Python, or PowerShell to control systems.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries attempt to gain access by trying multiple passwords or credentials until successful.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Attackers use stolen or legitimate credentials to gain unauthorized access to systems.

name: Drive-by Compromise
description: Users are compromised simply by visiting a malicious or vulnerable website.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
description: Attackers exploit vulnerabilities in client-side software like browsers or plugins to execute code.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries scan networks to discover services running on remote systems.

name: Exploitation of Remote Services
description: Attackers exploit vulnerabilities in remote services to gain unauthorized access.

name: Active Scanning
description: Attackers actively scan targets to identify vulnerabilities and open ports.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
description: Adversaries compromise software supply chains to distribute malicious code.

name: Credential Dumping
description: Attackers extract credentials from operating systems or applications.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries trick users into revealing credentials or executing malicious files.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Attackers use common protocols like HTTP/HTTPS to communicate with compromised systems.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries obfuscate malicious code to evade detection.

name: Process Injection
description: Attackers inject code into legitimate processes to execute malicious actions.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries search for files and directories to identify sensitive data.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Attackers steal data by sending it over command and control channels.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service
description: Adversaries disrupt services by overwhelming systems with traffic or requests.

name: Credentials from Password Stores
description: Attackers extract credentials stored in browsers or applications.

name: Stage Capabilities
description: Adversaries prepare infrastructure and payloads before launching attacks.
